DURATION_MISMATCH: duration_days must be the ORIGINAL term. ValleyCentral's own headline and article confirm the Commission's May 20, 2026 action was a 120-day moratorium; the subsequent 60-day extension (reported by KRGV, first reading ~Aug. 13/25, second reading ~2 weeks later) brought the TOTAL to the 180-day statutory maximum, already captured in current_end_date_iso=2026-12-16, but is not itself the original term.

Ordinance No. 26-1258's own text (Section 3) states the extension 'will remain in effect for a period of six (6) months from the effective date of this Ordinance' and (Section 8) is an emergency ordinance effective immediately upon passage. The ordinance's adoption/signature block reads (OCR-garbled) 'ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL AT A REGULAR MEETING THEREOF ON THE [1ST] DAY OF SEPTEMBER, 2026,' which a Facebook post from the city government confirms was a Sept. 1, 2026 council meeting. 2026-09-01 plus six months is 2027-03-01.

The primary 2018 news report of the ordinance's passage states its operative scope explicitly: 'The moratorium strictly prohibits new cryptocurrency mining operations, along with data centers and server farms/clusters, in all zones in the city, with the exception of the light industrial and heavy industrial zones.' This matches the row's own legal_basis, which already describes Ordinance 2900 as 'a moratorium on cryptocurrency mining, server farms, and data centers.'

The signed Ordinance No. 02-2026 states 'EFFECTIVE: April 25, 2026' and Section 2 renews the moratorium 'for a period of six months from the effective date of this ordinance.' 2026-04-25 plus six months is 2026-10-25.

Ordinance No. 2833's own text states the moratorium 'shall be extended for twelve (12) additional months from the expiration date of Ordinance 2806 (expiration February 24, 2026).' 2026-02-24 plus 12 months is 2027-02-24, matching the row's own estimate.
